candidates.name: Nuremberg Castle
candidates.price: Castle €10, concessions €9, under-18s free; combi with Cadolzburg Castle €16 (conc €14)
candidates.content: The Nuremberg Castle is the rambling fortification that dominates the old town. While it appears to be one massive fortress, it historically consists of three distinct parts that often stood in conflict with one another.

candidates.name: Verkehrsmuseum
candidates.content: This museum contains two collections: the DB Museum (DB National Railway Museum) and the Museum for Communication. The railway museum explores the history of railways in Germany from 1835 - when the first railway connecting Nuremb

candidates.name: Museum of Industrial Culture
candidates.content: Set in an old screw factory, the last remnant of the sprawling Tafel metalwork complex. Tells the story from the Industrial Revolution into the early 20th century. Along a museum street you see how living conditions, social life a

candidates.name: Memorium Nuremberg Trials and Courtroom 600
candidates.content: After World War II, this site was chosen for trials of the Nazi high command, partly for Nuremberg's symbolic role in Nazism, but chiefly because the Palace of Justice was undamaged and contained a prison block. Charges were broug

candidates.name: Historic tram depot (Historisches-Straßenbahndepot)
candidates.hours: Every first full weekend of the month, Sat Sun 10:00-17:00
candidates.content: Trams since they began here in 1881. Several are in working order and when the museum is open, they make a leisurely grinding circuit of the city's public tramways.

candidates.name: Deutsches Spielearchiv Nürnberg
candidates.content: A museum dedicated to preserving the history of board games with many original games, some of which can be played by visitors. If you intend to write academically about board games, this is a place with countless resources at your

candidates.name: Tower of the Senses
candidates.content: Interactive science museum with emphasis on human perceptionClosed during Winter (17 Dec to 1 Mar)

candidates.name: St Lawrence Church
candidates.content: Mostly built in the 15th century and now part of the Evangelical or Lutheran church of Germany, Lorenzkirche forms the focus of the south-side old town. It's dominated within by the 18m tall Tabernacle, a Gothic spire made circa 1

candidates.name: Way of Human Rights
candidates.content: A monumental outdoor sculpture, opened on 24 October 1993. It is sited on the street between the new and old buildings of the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, connecting Kornmarkt street and the medieval city wall.

candidates.name: Neunhof Manor, (Schloss Neunhof)
candidates.content: Nuremberg's patricians had numerous manor houses in the surrounding villages. This is a good example, built in the 16th century. Adjoining is a small baroque garden. The castle is closed for renovation in 2017.

candidates.name: Albrecht Dürer's House
candidates.price: Adults €7.50, children: €2.50, with Nürnberg-Pass, Fürth-Pass, Erlangen-Pass und Schwabach-Pass: €2.00
candidates.hours: Tue Wed Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat Sun 10:00-17:00. Mon only open July-Sept & for Christmas Market, 10:00-17:00
candidates.content: The house in which the painter Albrecht Dürer lived and worked from 1509 until 1528. Representative of a wealthy house of that period. Exhibition about life in the house and the way Dürer worked.

candidates.name: Documentation Centre at the Reich Party Rally Grounds
candidates.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, Sat Sun 10:00-18:00; allow 2 hours to visit
candidates.content: Soon after they came to power in 1933 the Nazis chose Nuremberg as the place for their annual party rallies. They planned a set of gigantic buildings here, few of which were built. Start at the Documentation Centre for the story o

candidates.name: Zoo (Tiergarten)
candidates.price: Adult €13.50, child €6.50, adult with Bahnpass €11.50, child with Bahnpass €4.80, Family with one adult €18, Family with 2 adults €31.50
candidates.content: The Nuremberg Tiergarten is one of the most beautiful zoos in Europe, set in forests and old quarries to the east of the city. Includes a Dolphinarium with regular shows.

candidates.name: Toy Museum
candidates.price: Adults: €7.50, children: €2.50, with Nürnberg-Pass, Fürth-Pass, Erlangen-Pass und Schwabach-Pass: €2.00
candidates.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat Sun 10:00-18:00; Mon only during Christmas Market 10:00-17:00; extended hours during Toy Fair
candidates.content: Nuremberg was one of the centres of the German toy industry. The exhibition shows wooden and metal toys, dolls and doll houses, model railways and modern toys.

candidates.name: Museum Tucherschloss and Hirsvogelsaal
candidates.content: The Tuchers and the Hirsvogels were wealthy trading families. This castle built between 1533 and 1544 shows their life in that era, with several original features.

candidates.name: St Sebald Church
candidates.content: Built in Romanesque style from the 13th century, with many later Gothic and Baroque additions, and now part of the Evangelical or Lutheran church of Germany, St Sebaldhus is the focus of the north-side old town. In the centre of t

candidates.name: Natural History Museum
candidates.content: The ground floor is the ethnology collection: masks from the South Seas, Costa Rican culture, a Berber tent from Morocco, and strange garb of the Nivchi, a Siberian people. The upper floor covers geology, prehistory and archaeolog

candidates.name: Nassauer Haus
candidates.content: Often cited as the oldest residential building in the city, its Romanesque cellars date back to the 12th century, while the upper structure is a prime example of late Gothic architecture. This distinctive medieval tower-house is f

candidates.name: Kunsthalle
candidates.content: Hosts changing art exhibitions. Entry is free on Wednesdays, 18:00–20:00.

candidates.name: Germanisches Nationalmuseum
candidates.content: One of the largest museum of art and crafts in the German-speaking countries, with a collection ranging from pre-historic artefacts to 20th century art. Allow at least half a day.

candidates.name: Imperial Castle
candidates.content: The western and most prestigious part, grouped around the inner courtyard. It was the temporary residence of the Holy Roman Emperors. The ticket includes the Palas (residential building), the double chapel, and the Imperial Castle

candidates.name: Burgrave’s Castle
candidates.content: The central and oldest part. It was the permanent seat of the Burgraves (House of Hohenzollern) until it was destroyed in 1420. Today, you can see the Pentagonal Tower and the Walburgis Chapel. Their other residence, Cadolzburg (2

candidates.name: Fembohaus Citymuseum
candidates.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat Sun 10:00-18:00, during Christkindlesmarkt also Mon: 10:00-17:00
candidates.content: A merchant's house built about 1600, in late Renaissance style. Exhibition about the history of the city.

candidates.name: Deutsches Museum Nürnberg
candidates.price: Adults: 10,50 €, Children: 6,50 €, Familycard (max. 2 adults plus 4 children below 6 and 4 children between 6 and 17): €22.00
candidates.content: Nuremberg's newest and most futuristic museum with numerous installations, interactive activity stations and bookable laboratory offers.

candidates.name: Neues Museum ("New Museum", State Museum for Art and Design in Nürnberg)
candidates.price: Permanent collection €6, concessions €6, Sundays €1; under 18s free
candidates.hours: Tue Wed Fri Sat Sun 10:00-18:00, Thu 10:00-20:00, Mon closed
candidates.content: Within Old Town but in a striking modern building, the museum shows art and design from 1945 to today.

candidates.name: St Johannis Friedhof
candidates.content: 14th-century graveyard with many famous citizens, including Albrecht Dürer and Adam Kraft. In summer the gardens are a riot of roses and other colourful flowers. You can walk here along Johannisstraße but the street is mostly mode

candidates.name: Children's Museum (Kindermuseum)
candidates.content: Hands-on museum, with two permanent exhibitions: everyday life of your great-grandparents, and treasure chamber earth.

candidates.name: Kraftshof Village Church
candidates.content: In the Middle Ages, cities like Nuremberg were strongly protected by walls and castles, but villages lacked them. It was often impractical to build these around a straggling farm village, and the cities jealously guarded their rig

candidates.name: Blue Night (Blaue Nacht)
candidates.content: A night when museums, churches and other cultural institutions stay open till dawn. Along with art and light installations, music and performances in Nuremberg's old town streets. The next Blue Night is 1-2 May 2020.

candidates.name: Nuremberg Falcons
candidates.content: After finishing second in the 2018/2019 second division season they qualified for promotion to the first division on the court but were denied promotion due to their temporary home field not being up for first division standards a

candidates.name: Nurembergs Underworld (Nürnberger Felsengänge)
candidates.hours: Tours daily every hour or two, but in English only on Sat & Sun at 11:15
candidates.content: The sandstone bedrock of Nuremberg's castle hill is riddled with vaulted cellars and passageways. Mostly carved out in the 14th century, they include beer cellars, casemates, water conduits; in World War II they were used as air r

candidates.name: Medieval Dungeons
candidates.hours: Guided tour with a media guide (English, Spanish, Italian, German), daily at 11:00, 12:00, 13:00, 14:00, 15:00
candidates.content: Medieval prison and torture museum under the city hall. Accessible only by guided tour. Not suitable for children under 10 and those with mobility impairments.

candidates.name: Cinecitta
candidates.content: The biggest multiplex cinema in Germany. 18 movie theaters, one IMAX theater, one "motion action drive" cinema, three restaurants, twelve bars and five outside terraces with view on the historic town.

candidates.name: Langwasserbad
candidates.content: Large indoor swimming pool with sauna and wellness facilities. Bathing and wellness is mixed gender, use of the pool requires beach wear. No towels, slippers, or drinks included in the entrance fee so you'll need to supply these y

candidates.name: Panoptikum Children’s Theatre Festival (Kindertheaterfestival)
candidates.content: Wide-ranging programme with artistes from Bavaria and across Europe. Aimed at children 3 and older, i.e. verbal and in German, though some shows use little or no spoken language. This festival runs alternate years so the subsequen

candidates.name: Nuremberg Flea Market (Trempelmärkte)
candidates.content: Trödelmarkt on the little river island is the permanent flea market, but the event on the second weekend in May and on the first weekend in September takes over the entire Old Town, with 4000 booths. Children have their own free a

candidates.name: Rock im Park
candidates.content: Annual rock festival, featuring alternative rock, heavy metal, punk rock, & electronic music. It’s held simultaneously with the Rock am Ring festival at Nürburgring motor racing circuit, with most artistes appearing at both.

candidates.name: Norisring DTM Motor Racing (Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters)
candidates.content: DTM racing cars are touring cars - they look more like a “normal” road car than F1 racing cars do, being wider and heavier. They’re slower too but still mighty fast. There are ten races at various European circuits in the season,

candidates.name: Bardtreffen music festival
candidates.content: At various city venues, free.

candidates.name: Old Town Festival (Altstadtfest)
candidates.content: Two-week event in mid-September, with music and processions. There’s food and drink at the Gastronomy Market and at numerous restaurants and beer gardens in the old town centre.

candidates.name: Christmas Market
candidates.content: This is the big one, drawing large crowds from across Europe. Held from the Friday before the first advent Sunday to 23 December. Over 180 retail booths, and more gingerbread than you thought possible.

candidates.name: 1. FC Nuremberg
candidates.content: The club, founded in 1900, play football in the 2. Bundesliga, Germany's second division. In 2017 the stadium was renamed for famous player Max Morlock, but the S-bahn station still reflects a former name "Frankenstadion".

candidates.name: Arena Nürnberg Versicherung
candidates.content: A multipurpose sports venue next to the 1. FCN Max Morlock Stadium (same transport directions). They host: Thomas Sabo Ice Tigers who play ice hockey in the Deutsche Eishockey Liga, Germany's top league. Other teams (part of EHC 8

candidates.name: Nuremberg Spring Festival (Frühlingsfest)
candidates.content: Spring funfair held for two weeks in March/April. (“Volksfest” refers both to this spring festival, and the late summer festival in Aug/Sept.)

candidates.name: Figurentheaterfestival
candidates.content: Held in alternate years. The next starts in late May 2021.

candidates.name: Embedded World
candidates.content: One of the largest electronics shows in Europe, and a must see for anyone interested in high tech gadgets (robots, tablets, artificial intelligence, ...).

candidates.name: International Organ Week (Internationale Orgelwoche Nürnberg)
candidates.content: Festival of organ and other sacred music. The next festival runs from 26 June to 2 July 2020.

candidates.name: Open Air Classics
candidates.content: Concerts staged on two summer weekends, two weeks apart, in the park at Dutzendteich.

candidates.name: Mata Hari Bar
candidates.content: One of the places where it's easiest to get into conversations when you're coming by yourself. A small but atmosphere-packed place, where you can often hardly move but have great evenings talking about everyone and his brother.

candidates.name: Hannemann
candidates.content: A bar in between your grandma's style of living room (and similarly relaxed) and a hip modern place – if you want to chat with friends or just hang around easy-going people, that's one of the places you can choose.

candidates.name: Restaurant und Biergarten Kopernikus im Krakauer Haus
candidates.hours: summer Mon-Fri 16:00-00:00, Sat Sun holidays 12:00-00:00; winter Mon-Fri 17:00-00:00, Sat Sun holidays 12:00-00:00
candidates.content: A restaurant with a special beer garden which is nicely located on the city wall and also has tables along the city wall on a wooden path used with the fortification; the building housing the restaurant is a cultural centre connec

candidates.name: Gelbes Haus
candidates.content: This is a mid-sized bar with two rooms, one with wood coated walls (which are nevertheless not "too heavy) and another one with the actual bar in it and in the style of the building; they serve a huge variety of classical, well-pr

candidates.name: Club Stereo
candidates.content: A small, nice club with changing offers (music genre highly depending on what the current event is), regularly offering nice concerts, too. The club is located in the basement and shares its entrance with the bar Vorraum, which is

candidates.name: MUZclub
candidates.content: A live music-oriented club with a nice garden for warm summer evenings which is operated by the non-profit music supporting association "Musikzentrale Nürnberg e.V." which regularly hosts concerts ranging from local scene festival

candidates.name: Salon Regina
candidates.content: A café at day and a nice bar with a variety of people in the early evening - good to visit during daytime or to start your evening in Gostenhof.

candidates.name: Kater Murr
candidates.content: A friendly pub, with ties to the local creative scene, which regularly hosts exhibitions and from time to time other cultural events.

candidates.name: Kulturgarten
candidates.content: At the local cultural centre Künstlerhaus.

candidates.name: Schanzenbräu Schankwirtschaft
candidates.content: The beer garden of one of the hippest Nuremberg breweries. Serve delicious locally-brewed beer.

candidates.name: Cubano
candidates.content: Another good cocktail bar.

candidates.name: Mach 1
candidates.content: Nice club with good flair. They usually play House music.

candidates.name: Die Rakete
candidates.content: An institution in electronic music, this small but nice club is known well over the region.

candidates.name: Bratwursthäusle
candidates.content: Restaurant in the old city centre specializing in roasted sausages. You can see many tourists there as it's one of the most frequented places to have a "Bratwurst" (grilled sausage). One of the most common packages is "Drei im Wec

candidates.name: Red Curry House
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 11:30-20:30, closed on Sun and public holidays
candidates.content: South East Asian food, tasty, with very good value for price small dishes

candidates.name: Suppdiwupp
candidates.content: Great soups and hotpots served with fresh traditional style bread; the offerings change and there are not many dishes, but usually everybody should find something along her/his taste on the menu.

candidates.name: Restaurant Heilig-Geist-Spital
candidates.content: Mainly local cuisine. Historic dining room situated over the river Pegnitz.

candidates.name: Steichele, Hotel & Weinrestaurant.
candidates.content: Local cuisine. The Steichele has the opportunity to try, drink and buy selected wines from "Franken", the "Pfalz", "Südtirol" and many more producing regions of Germany.

candidates.name: Albrecht-Dürer-Stube
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 18;00-00:00, Fri Sun also 11:30-14:30; closed on Sun in June, July & August, warm dishes until 00:00
candidates.content: A very traditional Franconian restaurant, frequented by locals and tourists alike. It is a good choice if you want to have some hearty local food in an unpretentious atmosphere. As the venue is small and popular, it is often neces

candidates.name: Schlemmer Eck - Schlütter's Echte
candidates.content: The original Nuremberg sausages from the producer in the city. The place is hidden in a small lane.

candidates.name: Max Express
candidates.content: Turkey schnitzel and pizza are delicious. Staff very friendly.

candidates.name: Brezen Kolb
candidates.content: Brezen Kolb is the undisputed local hero in the Nuremberg pretzel business. Especially recommended with butter and chives.

candidates.name: Wurstdurst
candidates.content: Serving the typical German currywurst. Ambiance and food top notch. Cozy atmosphere and super friendly staff. Also offering a tasty vegan currywurst.

candidates.name: Bra Kebap
candidates.content: Good fresh ingredients. The dough for Dürüm is freshly prepared. You can choose between veal and chicken when it comes to meat.

candidates.name: Historische Bratwurstküche - Zum Guldenen Stern
candidates.content: Restaurant in an old timber-framed house specializing in roasted sausages. Oldest sausage restaurant in the world, since 1419. Located in a small pedestrian zone in the Lorenz district, near Jacobsplatz, walkable distance (ca. 10

december.text: When people think of Nuremberg, they usually think of gingerbread, toys, Christmas, the Reich Party Rally Grounds or the Nuremberg Trials (see World War II in Europe and Holocaust remembrance). But the old town of Nuremberg in the shadow of the towering imperial castle is more than that. Gothic churches, splendid patri

The big annual event in Nuremberg is the Christmas Market (Christkindlesmarkt), listed below. But there’s a full calendar throughout the year – check what’s on even if you don’t plan to attend, as there may be street closures and crowd congestion.

Christmas Market: This is the big one, drawing large crowds from across Europe. Held from the Friday before the first advent Sunday to 23 December. Over 180 retail booths, and more gingerbread than you thought possible.
